US.why: Held. On 30 Oct the S&P fell 1.82% to 7580.07, its worst day since June and a third weekly loss, the Nasdaq 2.86% to 25437.00 and the Dow 1.09% to 51770.31, as Intel had its worst day since 1974 on a weak forecast and Amazon's profit disappointed, a day after Alphabet's quarter revived the question of what the AI build-out earns. The economy is not the problem: GDP grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter against 3.1% expected, but September core PCE was 3.1% on the year and producer prices rose 1.3% in the month; 2 Fed voters wanted a hike on 28 Oct, FedWatch has one by December at 79.6% on 29 Oct, and the 10-year closed at 4.94% on 30 Oct. FactSet's 23 Oct count has 83% of reporting companies beating estimates and the index on 18.7x forward earnings, below its five- and ten-year averages. The consumer is the weak point: Michigan sentiment ended October at 48.0, the lowest since May, retail sales rose 0.8% in September, the saving rate down to 3.8%. The anchor holds at 6.5 on two structural points: the US is a net energy EXPORTER, a relative tailwind with Brent +79.3% y/y, and NDX at 22.4x forward on its last verified reading sat below its 10y and 5y averages. J.P. Morgan's 2027 assumptions lift US large caps to 7.5% from 6.7%; that is already in every US fund's base return, so it does not move the anchor as well. THREE YEARS: 5.5, a point below the 6.5 anchor. The Fed's own path keeps policy above its 3.2% long-run rate through all three - 4.1% at the end of 2026 and 2027, 3.9% at end-2028 - and the cyclically adjusted P/E is 40.7, against a 44.2 record and a 16.6 long-run median: a valuation that has historically cost the next years' returns, whatever the forward multiple says. Against them, earnings growing at a record pace and the energy-exporter edge. FIVE YEARS (years 4-5): 6.25, as policy reaches neutral (3.6% at end-2029) and the AI spending has either paid or been digested. Most houses' decade forecasts favour non-US over US equities on the same valuation.
US.summary: Held: the S&P fell 1.82% to 7580.07 on 30 Oct, its worst day since June, as Intel and Amazon disappointed, after GDP beat at 3.4%; FedWatch has a December hike at 79.6% on 29 Oct.

EUROPE.why: Held. The ECB held its deposit rate at 2.50% on 29 Oct, after the 10 Sep hike, with September inflation confirmed at 3.8% (energy 18.8%, core 2.5%), and made no commitment on December; Lagarde said she will step down early, in February. The 10-year OAT-Bund spread eased to 135.5bp on 14 Oct from about 140bp as the Assembly took up a budget meant to cut the deficit to 5.0% of GDP from 5.4%. Europe is the largest net energy importer here, facing Brent +79.3% y/y against IMF growth of 1.1% this year; the offset is real - at 15.4x forward it is the cheapest large market after Asia. THREE YEARS: 3.75. The largest energy importer pays the most while oil stays high - December 2027 Brent was quoted at $87.82 on 22 Oct (another table has $86.46) - and growth starts at 1.1% under an ECB that hiked into it (the IMF's October upgrade, too small to offset oil's new high); a 15.4x market is the offset. FIVE YEARS (years 4-5): 4.5, at the anchor, as the shock fades - on 15 Oct the Brent curve settled near $72.32 for December 2029 and $69.16 for December 2030.
EUROPE.summary: Held: the ECB kept its deposit rate at 2.50% on 29 Oct with inflation at 3.8%, and Lagarde will leave early.

ASIA.why: Held; the ten-year anchor at 7.0 since 21 Oct. The AI trade turned on Asia's chipmakers: on 30 Oct the KOSPI fell 3.48% to 5,730.74 and the Nikkei 2.12% to 63,290.11 after Alphabet's quarter, and the BoJ held at 1.25% with a hike flagged for December. On the 29th the KOSPI had slipped 1.24% as Samsung fell on its detailed quarter, while the Nikkei rose 1.10%; on the 28th the KOSPI jumped 6.63% as SK hynix reported a record quarter - operating profit of 83.3tn won, up 632% on a year - and about 100tn won of shareholder returns for 2026. The KOSPI is 18.2% below its 7003.74 close of 2 Oct. China grew 4.5% in the third quarter against 4.4% expected, on exports, but its official factory PMI fell back to 49.3 in October from 50.1, a third contraction in four months. The earnings did not break: TSMC's third-quarter profit rose 68.7% to a record, and Samsung's quarter was a record 107.4tn won. Oil is the importers' problem, Brent at $117.64, with the yen near 158.48. The anchor was cut because half its case was the base return: it cited J.P. Morgan's EM equity assumption as the highest of any equity block, but that assumption is the Asia fund's base, so it was counted twice - and the 2027 edition cuts it to 7.1% from 7.8%, below US large caps. What remains is valuation: 10.5x forward before the fall against consensus EPS growth of ~52% and ~28% is a two-decade-wide discount. THREE YEARS: 6.5, half a point below the 7.0 anchor - the October selling and an importer's oil bill weigh on the first years. FIVE YEARS (years 4-5): 7.0, at the anchor, as earnings that grew into a discounted multiple re-rate it.
ASIA.summary: Held: the KOSPI fell 3.48% to 5,730.74 and the Nikkei 2.12% to 63,290.11 on 30 Oct on the AI-spending scare, and China's factory PMI fell back to 49.3; the BoJ held at 1.25%.

PHILIPPINES.why: Held. BSP raised its policy rate 50bp to 5.50% on 22 Oct, twice the 25bp that 20 of 22 analysts expected - its fourth straight hike and the first half-point since February 2023 - and the 26 Oct auction repriced to it: 91-day bills jumped 63.2bp to 6.624%, 182-day bills 20.1bp to 6.43% and 364-day bills 13.9bp to 6.583%, the two longer tenors under-awarded. The peso, after a record 64.17 on 27 Oct, kept recovering to 63.74 on 30 Oct, 11 centavos stronger on the day, after the President signalled support and the Fed held - still a 7.77% loss of purchasing power against the dollar this year. Governor Remolona left the 17 Dec meeting open, and says BSP will not defend a level and intervenes only to cushion excessive moves. The PSEi fell 0.44% to 5680.35 on 30 Oct on oil and fears of renewed US strikes on Iran, before the 2 Nov holiday, after rising 0.92% on the 29th; its 2026 low is 5610.39, on 8 Oct. September inflation was 7.2%, core 4.7%: against it every tenor's real yield is still below zero, though the gap closed by up to 63bp in one auction. This sleeve's job - zero duration risk and high nominal carry - is unimpaired. Its purchasing power is not. THREE YEARS: 5.25. BSP sees inflation at 6.1% this year and 6.0% next, then 3.3% in 2028, inside its 2-4% target, while the IMF has growth recovering to 5.1% in 2027 from 3.4%: the real carry is about nil for two of the three years. FIVE YEARS (years 4-5): 5.75, a little above neutral, as a policy rate set against 6% inflation meets inflation back near 3%.
PHILIPPINES.summary: Held: the peso recovered to 63.74 on 30 Oct from its 64.17 record while the PSEi fell 0.44%; 91-day bills are at 6.624% after BSP's 50bp hike.

drivers.name: Monetary policy & liquidity
drivers.note: HELD at 2.0. The Fed held at 3.75-4.00% on 28 Oct, 10-2, Governor Cook and Cleveland's Hammack for a hike, and the statement calls inflation elevated. September's core PCE then rose 0.3% on the month and 3.1% on the year, headline 0.5% and 3.6%, and FedWatch has a hike by the 9 Dec meeting at 79.6% on 29 Oct, from 85% on the 28th. On official closes the 10-year was 5.05% on the 28th, 4.98% on the 29th and 4.94% on the 30th, as the tech sell-off sent money into Treasuries, with the 2-year at 4.56% (30 Oct) and the 30-year at 5.31% (30 Oct). The 10-year's 7 Oct intraday high of 5.365%, above the 5 Oct peak of 5.349%, was the highest since April 2002. The ECB held at 2.50% on 29 Oct and the BoJ, a day later, at 1.25%, 8-1 with a vote for 1.5% and a hike flagged for December. Manila repriced to BSP's 50bp hike to 5.50%: at the 26 Oct auction 91-day bills jumped 63.2bp to 6.624%, 182-day bills 20.1bp to 6.43% and 364-day bills 13.9bp to 6.583%. Held: the hold and a firm core were both in the December-hike path the score assumed.
drivers.summary: Held: September core PCE ran 3.1% on the year after the Fed held, and FedWatch has a December hike at 79.6% on 29 Oct; the ECB and the BoJ held too.
drivers.path_why: The Fed's own September path keeps its rate above the 3.2% it calls neutral for three years - 4.1% at the end of 2026 and 2027, 3.9% in 2028 - and BSP, hiking now, only hints at easing in 2027: 3.5 for years 1-3. Then 3.6% in 2029, close to neutral: 5.0 for years 4-5.

drivers.name: Inflation trajectory
drivers.note: HELD at 2.0. September PCE prices rose 0.5% on the month and 3.6% on the year, from 3.4% in August; core rose 0.3% and 3.1%, from 3.0%, in line with forecasts. That followed September PPI up 1.3%, the largest monthly rise since March 2022, and 6.3% on the year (core 0.5% and 5.0%), and CPI of 3.7% (core 2.6%). Brent settled at $117.64 on 30 Oct, up $2.76 on the December contract's last day, its highest close since the end of April, 0.8% higher on the week and 79.3% above the $65.62 of a year earlier; December WTI settled at $104.12 on 30 Oct. The euro area is at 3.8% (core 2.5%) and the Philippines at 7.2%. Held: core is firming, not running away, and most of the jump is energy passing through, not yet wages.
drivers.summary: Held: September PCE prices rose 3.6% on the year, core 3.1%; Brent settled at $117.64 on 30 Oct, +79.3% y/y.
drivers.path_why: BSP sees 6.1% this year and 6.0% in 2027 before 3.3% in 2028, and the US prices 2.37-2.48% a year over five years (October breakevens): 3.75 for years 1-3. The market puts the five after at about 2.2%, near target: 5.25 for years 4-5.

drivers.name: Growth momentum
drivers.note: HELD at 4.0. US GDP grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter, against 3.1% expected and 2.2% in the second, on inventories, equipment and consumer and government spending - but September's real spending was flat and the saving rate fell to 3.8%, the lowest in almost four years. China grew 4.5% on the year against 4.4% expected, on exports, but its September retail sales rose only 1.1% and its official factory PMI fell back to 49.3 in October, services and construction to 49.7 from 50.2. Michigan sentiment ended October at 48.0, revised up from a first read of 46.3 but the lowest since May's record low of 44.8; ISM services (54.9) and manufacturing (54.5) stayed in expansion in September. Philippine growth was 2.6% in the first half. Held: a beat built on inventories, with a stretched consumer behind it, is not a turn in the cycle.
drivers.summary: Held: US GDP grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter against 3.1% expected, on inventories, while September's real spending was flat.
drivers.path_why: The IMF has the world at 3.1% this year and 3.4% next and the Philippines recovering to 5.1% in 2027 but below its potential, with a hiking cycle and an energy shock in train: 4.5 for years 1-3, 5.25 for years 4-5 as policy turns.

drivers.name: Corporate earnings
drivers.note: HELD at 7.0, still the strongest pillar; the market is pricing the financing, not the profits. FactSet's 23 Oct count has 24% of the S&P reported and 83% beating estimates - by 2.1% in aggregate, against a 7.5% five-year average - with third-quarter growth blended at 29.5%, from 29.2%; health care is the one sector with earnings down on a year. On 29 Oct Alphabet took the largest one-day fall in market value in its history after a revenue miss and negative free cash flow on its AI spending, and the Nasdaq fell 1.38%; on the 30th the KOSPI fell 3.48% and the Nikkei 2.12%, then Intel had its worst day since 1974 on a weak forecast, Amazon's profit disappointed and the Nasdaq fell 2.86% more. The suppliers' numbers are records: SK hynix's third-quarter operating profit was 83.3tn won, up 632% on a year, with about 100tn won of shareholder returns planned for 2026; TSMC's net income rose 68.7% to NT$763.06bn, above the NT$746.34bn expected; Samsung's quarter was a record 107.4tn won. Asia ex-Japan EPS of ~+52% (2026) and ~+28% (2027) stands. Held: the profits keep coming; what is being questioned is the return on the spending that buys them.
drivers.summary: Held, the strongest pillar: 83% of reporting S&P companies beat (FactSet, 23 Oct), but the AI-spending scare took the Nasdaq down 1.38% on 29 Oct and 2.86% on 30 Oct.
drivers.path_why: Analysts' long-term S&P growth forecast is 16.7%, in the top tenth this century, and this quarter is growing at 29.5%: 6.5 for years 1-3. But since 1992 they forecast 22.3% a year and got 9.5%: neutral by years 4-5 as margins revert.

drivers.name: Valuation support
drivers.note: HELD at 8.0: FactSet had the S&P on 18.7x forward earnings on 23 Oct, below its five-year (19.8x) and ten-year (19.1x) averages and the 19.0x of 30 Sep. The S&P closed at 7580.07 on 30 Oct, 3.1% below its 7818.93 record of 6 Oct. Asia was on 10.5x forward before its October fall and is cheaper on the same earnings: the KOSPI closed at 5,730.74 on 30 Oct, 18.2% below its 2 Oct close. NDX at 22.4x forward on its last verified reading sat below its 10y (22.9x) and 5y (24.7x) averages - two newer readings disagree (20.5x and 23.3x) and are not carried; Europe is at 15.4x. Held: cheaper than its averages on the one multiple re-verified, and the rest only cheaper since.
drivers.summary: Held: the S&P is on 18.7x forward earnings, below its five- and ten-year averages; the KOSPI is 18.2% below its 2 Oct close.
drivers.path_why: Asia at 10.5x and Europe at 15.4x are cheap, and the S&P's forward multiple is below its averages, but on ten-year earnings the S&P is on 40.7, near the 44.2 record: 6.5 for years 1-3, neutral for years 4-5, where the base returns already price the starting multiple.

drivers.name: Volatility & risk appetite
drivers.note: HELD at 2.5. The VIX rose 12.91% to 19.42 on 30 Oct, after 1.71% on the 29th, as the tech sell-off deepened; it touched 23.93 intraday, past the 22.31 high of 16 Oct, but closed still under the long-run 19.5. Asia took the shock first: on the 30th the KOSPI fell 3.48%, tripping a sell-side sidecar, and the Nikkei 2.12%. No full futures strip after the 20 Oct settlements has been reached, so the curve stays quoted there - November 18.49 and December 18.7, above that day's spot, the ordinary upward slope - and mean-reverts to the long run beyond. Tested against that day's VIX3M of 18.99 it gives 18.29 at three months, 3.66% below, inside the 10% bound; the 5 Oct strip it replaced read 4.66% below on the same test. On forward vol the curve sits at 19.42, 0.08 below the long run. Held: the close is under the long run and 2.5 is the score the 23 Oct AI sell-off set; a spike that gave back most of its rise by the close tests that, it does not yet make a new regime.
drivers.summary: Held: the VIX rose 12.91% to 19.42 on 30 Oct and touched 23.93 intraday, but closed under its long-run 19.5.
drivers.path_why: The VIX curve's own 3-year implied volatility is a little under the long run, while the hiking cycle and the Gulf keep risk appetite below neutral: 4.5 for years 1-3, neutral for years 4-5.

drivers.name: Geopolitics & energy
drivers.note: HELD at 1.5; a tanker attack on 30 Oct is confirmed, but the last confirmed count of the barrels had not shrunk. On 30 Oct UKMTO reported explosives attached to a tanker off Khasab, Oman, and the British military said a tanker had caught fire after a small boat attached two explosives to it; Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed that tankers leaving by unauthorised routes had struck mines, which US Central Command, saying it had cleared the main transit routes, called false (CNBC; AP; Gulf News; Reuters). On the 28th the US had reportedly told Gulf states to prepare for a short, intense campaign against Iran after the 3 November midterms (the Wall Street Journal, via CNBC), and the Houthis claim new attacks on Saudi airports and oil facilities while Qatari mediators are in Tehran. Brent settled at $117.64 on 30 Oct, its highest close since the end of April. Read it on VOLUME, the measure this note goes by: Kpler had oil through Hormuz, with Gulf of Oman transfers, at about 14 mb/d in the week to 18 Oct, 82% of pre-war on preliminary figures, and the Gulf's exports by every route above 24 mb/d against 23.3 pre-war. A lower figure for a later week is in one report only and October's average differs by source, so neither is carried. On 22 Sep Saudi Arabia restarted the 1200 km East-West pipeline that bypasses the Strait, and the export volumes since bear out that it runs. Vessel counts disagree and are not supply: IMF PortWatch counted 4 transits on 18 Oct against an 85 baseline, a 95% drop; Lloyd's List Intelligence 14 a day in the week to 23 Aug, counting only cargo over 10000 dwt; the US government around 30, on a basis it does not state. Held, not cut: one confirmed attack is not a closure, and 1.0 is kept for full closure with Brent above $130 - strictly worse, and nearer than it was.
drivers.summary: Held: a tanker attack in Hormuz on 30 Oct is confirmed, but the last confirmed flows were near 14 mb/d; Brent settled at $117.64 on 30 Oct, its highest close since the end of April.
drivers.path_why: The oil market prices the shock out slowly: December 2027 Brent was quoted at $87.82 on 22 Oct (another table has $86.46), still far above pre-war - 3.0 for years 1-3. December 2029 settled at $72.32 and December 2030 at $69.16 on 15 Oct, against $105.92 for the front month: 5.0 for years 4-5, a premium still above pre-war.

dd_model.note: 1.65 is the calibration anchor, not the coefficient every sleeve uses. Each fund carries a declared adjustment for the shape of its own left tail; the portfolio coefficient is the weighted average across the equity sleeves. The whole quantity is then scaled by sqrt(horizon / calibration window), because expected maximum drawdown grows with the square root of the horizon - the -20% and -33% anchors are rolling FIVE-year medians and cannot simply be relabelled for a longer mandate.
